posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Lam Research and ASE expansions; data center shifts; CPO system architecture initiative; 2D-transistor interface solution; USENIX HW security; patent suits; image sensors; programmable AI memtransistor; Nvidia's new plan; earnings; Tier IV's L4 auto chip.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: ASE subsidiary SPIL is investing $3.1 billion in a new Taiwan-based facility to expand CoWoS capacity for AI chips, with production slated to begin in 2028.
Lam Research announced a $3 billion, five-year R&D expansion plan to increase its experimental capacity by over 50%, alongside a workforce development partnership with NY Creates.
Data center infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental shift toward 1-megawatt racks, necessitating significant changes in cooling, power delivery, and the integration of optical interconnects.

Rhodium Group projects that China will control nearly 50% of global legacy-chip capacity by 2030, as domestic equipment manufacturers continue to scale despite restrictions on leading-edge AI hardware.
Industry experts are increasingly advocating for smaller, open-source AI models that reduce the reliance on massive data centers by optimizing energy, water, and compute efficiency.

posts.title: Geely Farizon's first overseas plant starts operations in Indonesia
posts.summary:
The first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle rolled off the line on August 13 at a plant about 80 kilometers southeast of Jakarta.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: - The first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle rolled off the line on August 13 at a plant about 80 kilometers southeast of Jakarta.
- It is Geely Farizon's first overseas KD project, coming just months after the company entered Indonesia in January 2026.
Geely Farizon's KD (knock-down) plant in Indonesia has officially started operations, making it the first overseas localized production project for Geely's commercial new energy vehicle (NEV) unit.
The first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle rolled off the line at the plant on August 13, the company said on Friday, marking the project's entry into large-scale operation.
The plant is located about 80 kilometers southeast of Jakarta and can currently carry out local assembly of the V8E.

posts.title: Li Auto's L6 tops 400,000 cumulative deliveries as revamped model revives demand
posts.summary:
The Li L6 delivered about 9,000 units in the first half of August, compared with just 2,716 for the whole of July, based on CnEVPost-compiled data.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: - The Li L6 delivered about 9,000 units in the first half of August, compared with just 2,716 for the whole of July, based on CnEVPost-compiled data.
- In 2025, the Li L6 delivered 166,516 units, contributing 41% of the company's deliveries.
Li Auto (NASDAQ: LI) announced on Friday that cumulative deliveries of its Li L6 extended-range SUV (sport utility vehicle) have surpassed 400,000 units.
The model went on sale on April 18, 2024, meaning it took less than 27 months to reach the milestone.
As of the end of July, cumulative deliveries of the Li L6 stood at 391,002 units, according to CnEVPost-compiled data.

posts.title: Li Auto's chip ambitions extend from assisted driving to data centers, report says
posts.summary:
Li Auto is exploring an in-house cloud inference chip, and the project is still at an early stage.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: - Li Auto is exploring an in-house cloud inference chip, and the project is still at an early stage.
- Cloud inference chips can take on some of the inference workloads that currently run on GPUs.
Li Auto (NASDAQ: LI) is exploring an in-house cloud inference chip, according to a report on Friday by local media outlet LatePost.
The chip will use the same dataflow architecture as its assisted driving chip, and the project is still at an early stage, the report said, citing multiple sources.
AI (artificial intelligence) data centers generally use GPUs for model training and inference, though some also deploy dedicated cloud inference chips, the report noted.

posts.title: 2026.33: The CapEx Train Keeps Rolling
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of August 10, 2026, including the capital constraint, AI writing, and a tale of two cities.
bullets: Nvidia is implementing new financial engineering mechanisms to secure long-duration capital, signaling potential concerns about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.
The reliance on creative funding structures and equity taps by major players like Google suggests that AI compute investments are not yet generating sufficient organic returns to be self-funding.

New EU regulations mandating the labeling of AI-generated content face significant criticism for potentially stifling innovation and failing to account for evolving societal norms regarding synthetic output.

The divergence between New York City’s resilient financial sector and Hollywood’s declining production base highlights how network effects can be preserved in some industries while being easily disrupted in others.
